protests.name: IIT Delhi Student Protest Over Rishikesh Kumar Suicide Case
protests.location: IIT Delhi Main Gate, Hauz Khas, New Delhi
protests.cause: Students are protesting against the administration's handling of the suicide of 31-year-old MSc Physics student Rishikesh Kumar. They demand a transparent investigation, accountability for alleged administrative negligence, and concrete action on the issues of student mental health and academic pressure that they believe contributed to the tragedy.
protests.dangerReason: The protest has remained largely peaceful with no reports of police violence, mass detentions, lathi charges, or clashes in the available search results. Delhi Police have registered an FIR for abetment of suicide and an external inquiry committee was formed, indicating a formal process rather than active suppression. However, tensions persist due to the emotional intensity of the issue, the institute's warning of disciplinary action, and the midnight protest, creating potential for escalation if demands are not addressed.
protests.status: Over 500 IIT Delhi students, including many B.Tech students, have been protesting since 24 August 2026 over the death of 31-year-old MSc Physics student Rishikesh Kumar, who died by suicide on campus on 22 August. Students staged a sit-in at the main gate and held a midnight protest in residential areas, raising slogans and demanding justice, an independent probe, accountability, and action on student mental health. Delhi Police have registered an FIR for abetment of suicide, and an external inquiry committee was constituted, but its chairperson recused himself, prompting the institute to re-form the panel. Classes have been suspended, and students are also seeking Rs 1 crore compensation. The institute has warned of disciplinary action over alleged disruption, while students have vowed to continue until their demands are met.
details: Police presence: No specific police deployment numbers or equipment reported at IIT Delhi main gate; Delhi Police have registered an FIR for abetment of suicide, indicating investigation rather than crowd control.
Recent incidents: Protests continued on Day 4 (around 27-28 August 2026) with sit-ins and midnight demonstrations; no injuries, arrests, or property damage reported in available search results.
Medical access: No reports of injuries or medical access issues; campus mental health services are under scrutiny as part of protest demands, but no blockades or ambulance obstructions noted.

Legal support: Delhi Police FIR for abetment of suicide filed; external inquiry committee re-formed after chairperson recused; no specific legal aid organizations or helplines mentioned for detained protesters (none reported detained).

protests.name: CJP-Led Chalo Protest — Police Brutality Accountability Demand
protests.location: Jantar Mantar and surrounding areas, New Delhi
protests.cause: Protesters are demanding accountability for unlawful and deadly police force used against peaceful CJP-led 'Chalo' protests, including the use of pellets, grenades, tear gas, and electric shock devices against Gen-Z and student demonstrators.
protests.dangerReason: Documented use of lethal crowd-control weapons — tear gas, pellet guns, batons and electric shock devices — against unarmed CJP-led protesters in Delhi between June and July 2026, with the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' crackdown injuring 60 protesters and 118 police personnel, and CJP alleging female demonstrators were beaten by male officers. The August 2026 Amnesty International investigation found no disciplinary action against officers, indicating continued impunity, while mass detentions including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and the Supreme Court's formation of an investigation panel keep tensions elevated. Although organisers have halted further marches for now, any renewed gathering at Jantar Mantar could face severe suppression, keeping the risk level high rather than critical.
protests.status: The CJP-led 'Chalo' protest movement remains active around Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, with the July 20, 2026 'Chalo Sansad' march halted by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel using batons, tear gas, pellet guns and electric shock devices. Delhi Police reported 60 protesters and 118 of its own personnel injured amid stone-pelting allegations, while CJP claimed far higher protester injuries and accused male officers of beating female supporters. An August 2026 Amnesty International investigation documented unlawful and deadly force against peaceful CJP-led protesters between June and July 2026 with no disciplinary action against officers, and the Supreme Court has formed a panel to investigate allegations against both police and demonstrators. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke returned to the torn-down protest site near Jantar Mantar vowing to continue campaigning, but organisers have announced they will not stage another march through New Delhi for now, leaving the movement in a tense standoff rather than an active march.

Legal support: Supreme Court panel formed to investigate allegations against police and demonstrators; CJI Kant said no formal plea filed on police violence; Amnesty International documented unlawful force with no disciplinary action.

protests.name: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Anti-Election Commission Voter Roll Protest
protests.location: Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street, Central Delhi
protests.cause: Protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a mass voter-roll revision that has allegedly removed millions of eligible names from electoral rolls. The movement, led by the Gen Z 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), claims the revisions disproportionately exclude marginalized and opposition-leaning voters.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical due to the mass detention of over 7,500 protesters, including high-profile figures like CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, and Tushar Gandhi, on October 10, 2026, as reported by multiple sources. Delhi Police have imposed a strict lockdown, shut down 45 metro stations, cancelled trains, and deployed heavy barricades and personnel across the capital, effectively sealing off protest areas and limiting movement. The CJP claims over 15,000 detentions, indicating a massive punitive state response. The combination of city-wide lockdown measures, mass arrests, and the detention of key leaders creates a highly volatile environment with significant potential for further escalation and violence. The government's aggressive posture and the protesters' determination to continue until the CEC resigns suggest the situation will remain critical. The Supreme Court's intervention on October 11 to limit police action indicates ongoing legal tensions but does not immediately reduce the danger level.
protests.status: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) anti-Election Commission protest at Jantar Mantar, Central Delhi, remains active as of October 13, 2026, with the movement entering its second week. On October 10, Delhi Police detained over 7,500 protesters, including CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, and Tushar Gandhi, according to multiple reports. The CJP claims more than 15,000 detentions. Authorities imposed a strict city-wide lockdown, cancelling trains and metro services, erecting barricades, and deploying heavy police presence to seal off protest areas. On October 11, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi led a march to the Supreme Court in solidarity with detained protesters, and Congress MPs planned to meet over tea after the rally. On October 12, police detained CJP leaders again after they jumped barricades to enter a historic Delhi site. The protest, which began on October 3, demands the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a voter-roll revision that allegedly removed 130 million names. CJP leaders have accused the Modi government of creating an 'atmosphere of fear' and say India is 'at war with its citizens'. The movement has vowed to continue until the CEC resigns, and solidarity protests have emerged in Mumbai and Bengaluru. The situation remains highly volatile with no indication of de-escalation.

protests.name: Opposition Parties March to Election Commission
protests.location: Election Commission of India, Nirvachan Sadan, Ashoka Road, New Delhi
protests.cause: An alliance of India's opposition parties is launching protests under the banner 'Save Democracy' to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and to challenge alleged manipulation of voter lists that has removed millions of names. The march targets the Election Commission directly to demand transparency and restoration of excluded voters.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical because verified reports confirm that Delhi police detained more than 2,000 protesters on October 10, 2026, including the founder of the 'Cockroach' youth movement, and imposed a lockdown across the capital to prevent the protest. On October 12, police again obstructed protests by placing barricades around the Supreme Court as thousands of opposition demonstrators, led by Rahul Gandhi, attempted to march. On October 13, top leaders of the 'Cockroach' youth movement were detained after jumping barricades, indicating ongoing police action. Thousands of police officers and security personnel were deployed across central New Delhi for a third consecutive day, indicating sustained aggressive crowd control. The protest has been denied official permission, and previous reporting documented over 700 arrests at Jantar Mantar along with the brief detention of Rahul Gandhi and other opposition legislators. The combination of confirmed mass detentions, repeated police obstruction, heavy security deployment, and a denied-permission march creates a high risk of further clashes and arrests, justifying the critical designation.
protests.status: Thousands of opposition demonstrators, led by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, marched through central New Delhi on Monday, October 12, 2026, shifting their 'Save Democracy' agitation from the Election Commission to the Supreme Court. The march followed a weekend crackdown in which Delhi police detained more than 2,000 protesters on October 10, including the founder of the 'Cockroach' youth movement, and locked down the capital to prevent the planned protest at the Election Commission. On Monday, police again obstructed the protests, with barricades placed around the Supreme Court as thousands returned to the streets. The opposition petitioned the Supreme Court seeking suspension of voter list changes that removed over 130 million names, and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On Tuesday, October 13, top leaders of the 'Cockroach' youth movement were detained after they jumped barricades. Thousands of police officers and security personnel were deployed across central New Delhi for a third straight day. Rahul Gandhi compared the protests to 'tandav' and 'Shivji ki baraat', saying everyone is welcome. The opposition has vowed to continue the agitation despite mass detentions and police obstruction.

protests.name: Reservation Hatao Andolan at Jantar Mantar
protests.location: Jantar Mantar, Sansad Marg, New Delhi
protests.cause: Protesters under the banner 'Reservation Hatao Andolan' are demanding a complete overhaul and dismantling of India's caste-based reservation system in education and government employment, arguing it has failed its intended beneficiaries and entrenched caste divisions.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the Delhi Police's proactive detention of protesters for lacking permission, indicating a strict enforcement posture. The protest is highly polarizing, focusing on the abolition of caste-based reservations, which has historically sparked counter-mobilizations and communal tensions in Delhi. Police denied permission in advance, yet protesters gathered, leading to detentions, which could escalate if demonstrations continue. The location, Jantar Mantar, has been a flashpoint for police crackdowns on similar protests, including the use of force against CJP-led demonstrators in 2026. Although no violence was reported in the current incident, the potential for clashes or further detentions remains significant given the sensitive nature of the demands.
protests.status: The 'Reservation Hatao Andolan' protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, saw a sizeable gathering on Friday, August 21, 2026, with over 300 people associated with the movement assembling to demand the dismantling of caste-based reservation in education and government employment. Delhi Police had explicitly denied permission for the protest on Thursday, August 20, stating no authorization was granted for any demonstration on the issue. Despite the denial, protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar, prompting Delhi Police to detain several individuals for violating the permission requirement. Security was increased in the area, though no large-scale violence or injuries were reported. The movement is linked to an Instagram page campaigning against the UGC Act and SC/ST reservations, and organizers had raised a venue dispute between Jantar Mantar and Ramlila Maidan, but the gathering proceeded at Jantar Mantar. The protest appears to have been contained by authorities, with no immediate plans for further escalation announced. A viral video purportedly showing the protest was later debunked as old footage from the Jagannath Rath Yatra in Puri, Odisha.
details: Police presence: Delhi Police were deployed at Jantar Mantar on August 21, 2026, with security increased in the area. No specific numbers or equipment like water cannons or drones were mentioned in reports, but detentions occurred.

Recent incidents: On August 21, 2026, Delhi Police detained several protesters at Jantar Mantar after hundreds gathered for the 'Reservation Hatao Andolan' despite permission being denied. No injuries or property damage were reported.

protests.name: Anti-Police Brutality March at India Gate After Pellet Gun Injuries
protests.location: India Gate, Rajpath (Kartavya Path), Central Delhi
protests.cause: Protesters are demanding accountability after Delhi Police allegedly used metallic pellet guns against peaceful CJP demonstrators, causing severe eye and facial injuries. They are also calling for the suspension of officers involved and an independent judicial inquiry into police impunity.
protests.dangerReason: Multiple protesters have sustained severe pellet-like injuries, including a Delhi University student who may lose an eye and artist Prashant Kumar Singh, the fifth confirmed case, with police records confirming at least two rounds of pellets were used on July 20 on a DCP's orders. The Supreme Court has had to intervene, forming a probe panel and ordering no coercive action against youth protesters and the release of arrested minors, confirming that detentions and police action were serious enough to require judicial restraint. With CJP calling for another march on September 5, the government refusing to register FIRs against officers, and four FIRs already filed against protesters, the risk of renewed violent crackdowns, mass detentions and further injuries remains high.
protests.status: The anti-police brutality mobilisation at India Gate and Jantar Mantar continues, with several hundred protesters, mostly students and CJP supporters, demanding accountability for pellet-gun injuries allegedly inflicted during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march. Delhi Police publicly deny using pellet guns and shock batons, calling the claims 'fake news,' even as police records confirm at least two rounds of pellets were fired on July 20 on the orders of a deputy commissioner. A fifth pellet-injury case has emerged, that of Delhi artist Prashant Kumar Singh, who was hit during the Jantar Mantar protest. The Supreme Court has formed a probe panel into allegations of police violence, ordered no coercive action against youth protesters, and directed the release of arrested minors. Delhi Police have registered four FIRs in connection with the protest and are probing an alleged conspiracy, while CJP has called for a fresh march in Delhi on September 5, accusing the Centre of reneging on promises made on July 25.

Recent incidents: At least two rounds of pellets were used on July 20 on a DCP's orders; a fifth pellet-injury case, artist Prashant Kumar Singh, was reported from the Jantar Mantar protest.
Medical access: Injured protesters, including a Delhi University student who may lose an eye, have been treated at nearby hospitals; no reports of medical access being blocked.

The sit-in also demands the release of detained CJP activists and an end to police surveillance of protest organizers.
protests.dangerReason: The situation remains high-risk due to a documented July 20 police crackdown in Delhi against the Cockroach movement, which was followed by solidarity protests nationwide that were met with repression and police action in Bihar and Goa. The movement has explicitly cited police violence as a grievance, and opposition parties have shut down parliament over the government's handling of the protests, indicating a deeply hostile state posture. The government has labeled the movement 'anti-democratic,' and Delhi Police have previously confined protesters behind barricades, seized equipment, and detained organizers at Jantar Mantar. While the Education Minister's resignation represents a concession, the government has simultaneously offered fast-track courts that protesters rejected, and the CJP has called for further nationwide protests on July 24, signaling continued escalation potential. The combination of active police crackdowns, mass mobilization, and unresolved core demands keeps the risk of further clashes and detentions elevated.
protests.status: The Mumbai-New Delhi Cockroach Movement solidarity sit-in at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi remains active, with crowds of supporters continuing to gather at the protest site as part of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) agitation. The movement, which began just over two months ago as a satirical online campaign, has grown into a significant real-world political force, drawing hundreds of youth to solidarity actions in cities including a large gathering at T Nagar in Chennai. On July 20, a federal minister reportedly promised talks on the movement's demands, but protesters rejected the government's offer of fast-track courts for exam leaks as inadequate. Opposition MPs have disrupted and shut down parliament for multiple days in solidarity with the protesters, calling on the Modi government to address police violence and education scandals. The CJP has formally called for nationwide protests on July 24, indicating the movement intends to escalate rather than wind down. The sit-in at Jantar Mantar continues to press demands including the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner and the release of detained activists. The situation remains fluid, with no reports of the protest concluding.

protests.dangerReason: The danger level is assessed as high because, while Mumbai Police denied permission for the protest and the Bombay High Court refused to stop the march, there are no confirmed reports of police violence, mass detentions, or protester injuries in the current intelligence. The primary risk stems from Jarange's deteriorating health during his extended hunger strike, now past its 19th day, with reports indicating he needs ICU care but is heading to Mumbai despite severe dehydration. The government's outreach through CM Fadnavis and Minister Bawankule's appeal to avoid Mumbai during Ganeshotsav indicates an attempt to de-escalate, but Jarange's allegation of a conspiracy to kill him and his vow to proceed despite police denial sustain a tense standoff. The potential for confrontation remains if the march proceeds to Mumbai without permission, especially given the history of the city grinding to a halt during previous Maratha quota protests. However, the absence of actual violence or detentions keeps the level at high rather than critical.
protests.status: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange Patil's agitation remains active as of mid-September 2026, with his hunger strike now past its 19th day and his health severely deteriorated. Mumbai Police denied permission for his indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan on September 13, 2026, but the Bombay High Court declined to issue a prohibitory order against his proposed march, affirming protest as a fundamental right. Jarange has alleged a conspiracy to kill him during the Mumbai march. Despite police denial and health warnings, Jarange has vowed to proceed, creating a tense standoff with no reports of violence or mass detentions so far.

protests.name: Jadavpur University FETSU Clash and Student Protest
protests.location: Gate 4 of Jadavpur University, Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Road, Jadavpur, South Kolkata
protests.cause: Protesting against the forced cancellation of the FETSU (Faculty of Engineering and Technology Students' Union) meeting and alleged police brutality against students, with ABVP and Left-affiliated students demanding the right to hold democratic student union meetings without administrative or police interference.
protests.dangerReason: Multiple independent reports confirm actual physical violence between rival student groups at Jadavpur University on 19-20 August 2026, not merely tension: ABVP and Left-leaning (SFI/DSF) students clashed during a FETSU general body meeting, with several students from both camps injured and hospitalised at KPC Medical College Hospital. Reports describe stone-pelting, arson, vandalism, torn posters, and flags being set on fire, with clashes spilling onto the streets near Gate 4 where ABVP protesters breached barricades and clashed with police. A complaint naming 11 people was filed, and both blocs accused each other of bringing outsiders onto campus, raising the risk of renewed confrontation. The university has been closed indefinitely and the Vice Chancellor was hospitalised after falling ill during a meeting on the unrest, underscoring the severity. With rival groups planning further demonstrations and a probe committee only now beginning its work, the potential for fresh violence remains high.
protests.status: Jadavpur University in South Kolkata remains tense after a violent clash between ABVP and Left-leaning (SFI/DSF) student groups that erupted late on 19 August 2026 during a FETSU general body meeting near Gate 4 on Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Road, continuing past midnight into 20 August. Several students from both camps were injured and admitted to KPC Medical College Hospital, with reports of stone-pelting, arson, vandalism, torn posters, and flags set on fire; both sides accused each other of bringing outsiders onto campus. Fresh clashes spilled onto the streets on 20 August as ABVP protesters breached barricades at Gate 4 and clashed with police, and the BJP publicly distanced itself from the RSS-backed student body. Police were deployed outside the university after authorities sought assistance, and additional security forces remained around the campus amid fears of further clashes. A complaint naming 11 people was filed, and rival student organisations planned demonstrations around the university and the 8B Bus Stand. A probe committee constituted by the university is scheduled to hold its first meeting this week after the Vice Chancellor, who had fallen ill during a meeting on the unrest, rejoined. No negotiated settlement or formal conclusion of the FETSU dispute has been announced.

protests.location: Multiple locations across Kolkata including state secretariat area, major road intersections, and railway tracks near Sealdah and Howrah stations
protests.cause: Protesting against alleged non-payment and severe delays in disbursement of Annapurna Yojana food security benefits to elderly beneficiaries across West Bengal, demanding immediate release of pending funds and accountability from the state food and supplies department.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to active disruption of public infrastructure, including road and railway blockades by protesting women across multiple districts in West Bengal, as reported within the last 1-3 days. Protesters have stormed Seva Setu camps and allegedly damaged camp property, indicating a heightened risk of confrontations with authorities. The involvement of a Block Development Officer's alleged objectionable remarks in Malda district adds a volatile dimension. While no police violence or mass detentions are explicitly reported, the pattern of targeting government camps and blocking critical transport routes poses significant safety and legal risks. The state's acknowledgment of 1.58 crore transfers for September, alongside unresolved Aadhaar-bank linkage issues, suggests the agitation may persist.
protests.status: Protests over delayed and non-payment of Annapurna Yojana food security benefits continue across West Bengal, with women beneficiaries blocking roads, railway tracks, and disrupting government offices in Kolkata and other districts. The agitation has spread to multiple locations, including near Sealdah and Howrah stations, where railway tracks were blocked, and confrontations with political leaders have occurred. In Harishchandrapur, Malda district, women blocked roads after a Block Development Officer allegedly made objectionable remarks. The state government claims it has processed 1.58 crore transfers for September, but beneficiaries say they have not received the promised Rs 3,000 monthly assistance. Opposition leaders have blamed each other for the delays, with Mamata Banerjee accusing the BJP of breaking promises and BJP leaders citing system problems and sabotage. The protests show no signs of abating, with beneficiaries demanding immediate release of pending funds and accountability from the state food and supplies department.

protests.location: College Street to Lalbazaar (Kolkata Police Headquarters), stopped at Bentinck Street crossing, central Kolkata
protests.cause: Protesting alleged atrocities against Congress workers attacked en route to the July 21 Martyrs' Day rally, the eviction of hawkers, and police action against students. Demanding an impartial inquiry by Police Minister Suvendu Adhikari into the July 21 violence.
protests.dangerReason: The August 5, 2026 march remained largely peaceful, with no reports of injuries, arrests, or violence during the event, and police halted the procession with barricades at Bentinck Street crossing without any physical confrontation. However, underlying tensions persist over the July 21 Martyrs' Day rally where multiple Congress workers were allegedly attacked and hospitalized, as well as ongoing hawker evictions and police action against students. The lack of an impartial inquiry into the July 21 violence keeps confrontation risk elevated despite the restrained nature of this particular protest.
protests.status: On Wednesday, August 5, 2026, hundreds of Congress leaders and workers, including AICC in-charge Prakash Joshi and West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar, took out the 'Lalbazaar Satyagraha' march from College Street toward Kolkata Police headquarters at Lalbazaar. Kolkata Police erected heavy barricades and halted the procession roughly a kilometre from the police headquarters at the Bentinck Street crossing in central Kolkata, where protesters staged a sit-in demonstration. The march protested alleged atrocities against Congress workers attacked en route to the July 21 Martyrs' Day rally, the eviction of hawkers, and police action against students, with leaders demanding an impartial inquiry by Police Minister Suvendu Adhikari into the July 21 violence. A separate Congress satyagraha was also held at the Calcutta University gate against alleged attacks on party workers. No further march dates have been announced, though Congress has signaled continued agitation over hawker evictions and worker safety.

The combination of active police violence, mass crowd size, and the charged political context following the Delhi police action on the 'Sansad Chalo' march creates a highly volatile environment with significant potential for further escalation and injuries.
protests.status: The GenZ Student Solidarity Protest March in Kolkata remains an active and volatile mobilisation, with the most recent confirmed escalation occurring on Friday, July 24, 2026, when violent clashes erupted in the Esplanade area during a CJP-Left students' rally. Thousands of students, starting from Sealdah and marching toward Esplanade, were met with police force as tear gas and batons were used to disperse crowds, leaving several people injured. The rally, which was denied police clearance and merged with a Leftist students' march, blocked central roads for hours and saw protesters demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak. Kolkata Police maintained a heavy presence along the route, and the event transformed from a solidarity march into a broader youth-led rebellion against repression. With train services scheduled to resume normal operations on October 11, the immediate disruption may ease, but the underlying tensions and legal challenges remain unresolved.
protests.status: Indian Railways cancelled multiple Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations on October 10 ahead of a proposed CJP protest in Delhi, disrupting services connecting Bhopal with the national capital. At Bhopal Junction and Rani Kamlapati (Habibganj) station, passengers faced long queues for refunds and alternative arrangements, while RPF personnel managed crowds on key platforms. Four Telangana Express passengers bound for the protest were deboarded at Bhopal station, and authorities also stopped 15 Pune students travelling to Delhi, with detentions reported at Bhopal, Itarsi and Gwalior. Madhya Pradesh Police detained 14 AISF students heading to Delhi for the CJP protest, citing 'orders from above' and questioning permissions for protests. The Madhya Pradesh High Court took note of two women detained en route after habeas corpus petitions were filed, and the Additional Advocate General issued an urgent communication to senior police officials. Train services are scheduled to return to normal on October 11, but traveller associations continue to demand special trains or alternative arrangements.

Protesters argue the cancellations stranded hundreds of Bhopal passengers and were imposed without consultation or alternative arrangements.
protests.dangerReason: The protest is centred on a busy railway station where large, frustrated crowds of stranded passengers can rapidly swell and block platform access and ticketing counters. Railway Protection Force and Government Railway Police have been deployed at Bhopal Junction with barricades at entry gates, and any attempt to occupy tracks or halt trains would sharply escalate the situation. No injuries or arrests have been reported so far, but the combination of cancelled services, angry travellers and a politically charged national protest theme keeps the risk of flash confrontation with police elevated.
protests.status: Around 150-200 protesters, including affected passengers, student groups and local activists, gathered outside Bhopal Junction's main entrance on the morning of 10 October 2026, holding placards against the train cancellations linked to the CJP's Jantar Mantar demonstration. Western Railway, North Western Railway and West Central Railway had cancelled multiple Delhi-bound services, leaving Bhopal travellers without alternatives on short notice. Government Railway Police and RPF personnel were stationed at the station's gates and foot overbridge, with barricades restricting access to platform one. Protesters submitted a memorandum to the station superintendent demanding restoration of cancelled trains and advance notice for future cancellations. Organisers have announced they will continue sit-ins at the station until railway authorities issue a written assurance on passenger compensation and scheduling.

Several protesters have been on hunger strike for over five days, with doctors monitoring their health. Police have detained protesters on multiple occasions when they attempted to march to the Secretariat. The protesters are demanding that the government formally communicate its anti-NEET resolution to the Centre and take concrete legal steps. Student organisations and political groups have extended support, and the protest is expected to grow.

protests.cause: Opposition to the University Grants Commission (UGC) new regulations (draft UGC (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment and Career Advancement of Teachers and other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education) Regulations, 2025) which the Rajput community claims dilute reservation, particularly for OBC, SC, ST, and EWS categories, and undermine the historical rights of Rajput youth in education and employment.

On August 3, 2026, Jaipur Police used a lathi-charge and water cannons on Karni Sena activists during a protest march against UGC Regulations 2026, and clashes occurred when protesters breached barricades near Statue Circle. A protester died amid the agitation, as reported by the Indian Express, marking a severe escalation. The Karni Sena has alleged the death was due to police action and is demanding compensation and suspension of involved personnel. The group has issued an ultimatum threatening a Jaipur bandh and a siege of the Chief Minister's residence, indicating further potential for unrest. The combination of a protester death, active police crackdown, and planned escalation creates a highly dangerous environment.

According to multiple reports, police used a lathi-charge and water cannons to disperse activists who had gathered in large numbers. The SRKS claims that a protester died from injuries sustained during the police action, and has demanded compensation, a government job for the deceased's family, and suspension of the personnel involved. The agitation is part of a larger 'Savarna Nyay Yatra' that began nearly 24 days ago, starting from Jaipur to Deshnok in Bikaner district. Karni Sena chief Mahipal Singh Makrana has issued an ultimatum threatening further action, including a Jaipur bandh and a siege of the Chief Minister's residence, and has threatened to withdraw support from the BJP. The situation remains volatile with no clear resolution in sight.

protests.cause: Protesting the power failure that disrupted the NEET-PG 2026 examination at two Jaipur centres on August 30, 2026, demanding accountability from NBEMS and fair retest arrangements for affected candidates.
protests.dangerReason: The protest remained largely peaceful with no reports of police violence, mass detentions, or clashes. Police presence was maintained at exam centres during the initial protest on August 30, 2026, and officers asked demonstrators to disperse, but no arrests or use of force have been reported. The government's rapid response, including forming a three-member committee and scheduling a timely retest, indicates authorities are managing the situation without confrontation, though tensions persist among affected candidates awaiting investigation results and compensation.
protests.status: The NEET-PG 2026 power failure protest in Jaipur has largely subsided following the retest conducted on September 5, 2026. Police personnel asked demonstrators to disperse, but no force was used. NBEMS constituted a three-member committee to investigate the internal power supply failure and scheduled a re-examination for 2,445 affected candidates on September 5, 2026, at 3 PM in Jaipur, which has since been conducted. Protesting students continue to demand compensation for travel and accommodation costs, transparency in the investigation findings, and assurance that the retest will not disadvantage them. No new protests or escalations have been reported since the retest.

protests.name: JDA Anti-Encroachment Drive Protest on New Sanganer Road
protests.location: New Sanganer Road, Jaipur (near Mansarovar and Sanganer areas)
protests.cause: Residents and shopkeepers are protesting the Jaipur Development Authority's demolition drive that began on August 24, 2026, targeting illegal constructions along New Sanganer Road. Affected families and business owners demand rehabilitation, compensation, and a halt to demolitions affecting over 250 structures.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical due to the massive deployment of 3,000 police personnel, drone surveillance, and a complete internet shutdown imposed across affected areas of Jaipur, indicating extreme measures to suppress dissent and control information. The ongoing demolition of over 260 structures, with traders claiming up to 750 shops and 3,000 families affected, has sparked continuous protests, including shop shutdowns, marches, tyre burning, and road blockades, creating a highly volatile environment. The Rajasthan High Court's order to widen the road to 160 feet means the drive is legally mandated, reducing the likelihood of it being halted and increasing the potential for confrontations. Protesters have physically attempted to block machinery and halt marking drives, raising the risk of clashes, injuries, and mass detentions. The combination of heavy police presence, communication blackout, and large-scale displacement poses a severe threat to public safety and order.

Protesters have employed tactics such as burning tyres, blocking the road, and shutting shops, and they successfully halted a JDA marking drive at one point. Tensions remain high as both sides refuse to back down, and no formal resolution or end to the protest has been announced.

The situation is politically charged, with Congress demanding withdrawal of orders and BJP accusing CJP of spreading anarchy. Local residents and CJP supporters continue to demand expedited construction and accountability. Police presence remains heavy to prevent further violence.

However, the session was adjourned in just 21 minutes on the opening day, indicating severe legislative disruption and escalating political tension between BJP and Congress. Media entry curbs raise concerns about transparency and could trigger larger street demonstrations if the impasse continues, with potential for confrontations between party workers outside the Assembly.

Police have maintained a presence around the Assembly complex in Jyoti Nagar, with barricades restricting movement near entry gates. The Congress has signaled it will continue the boycott and protest until media access is restored, and further adjournments are expected in coming sessions.

protests.name: Cockroach Janta Party Hunger Strike Over Voter List
protests.location: Outside Cockroach Janta Party founder's residence/office, Ahmedabad
protests.cause: Two youths from Ahmedabad are demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner over alleged irregularities in the voter list. They are protesting under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party and have initiated an indefinite hunger strike.
protests.dangerReason: The situation remains critical due to mass detentions and heavy police crackdown. Over 70 protesters were detained in Ahmedabad, including women, journalists, and seniors, and activists allege further detentions. In Delhi, chaos erupted as protesters tried to reach Jantar Mantar, and high-profile leaders like Neha Bora were detained. The active enforcement of restrictions and widespread detentions indicate a severe crackdown with a high risk of further escalation and potential violence. Although a court released some leaders on October 11, 2026, the protest continues and police posture remains aggressive.
protests.status: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) hunger strike in Ahmedabad, led by two youths demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter list irregularities, remains ongoing outside the CJP founder's residence/office. Ahmedabad police have detained over 70 protesters, including women, journalists, and senior citizens, in connection with the protest, and activists allege further detentions. The movement has spread nationwide: hundreds protested in Mumbai, with celebrities like Shabana Azmi, Vishal Bhardwaj, and Vishal Dadlani joining at Shivaji Park; in Delhi, chaos erupted as protesters tried to reach Jantar Mantar, and AISA president Neha Bora was detained near INA market. On October 11, 2026, a court released the CJP founder and two other leaders from detention. Opposition lawmakers disrupted parliament on Wednesday in support of the protesters. The indefinite hunger strike continues, and no resolution has been reached.

protests.cause: Protest against the removal of Malala Yousafzai's memoir and Anne Frank's diary from school reading lists, and against the FIR filed against 20 individuals including students and organizers after a silent reading session was disrupted by VHP/Bajrang Dal activists.
protests.dangerReason: The protest was physically attacked by alleged VHP/Bajrang Dal activists, resulting in injuries and a hostile environment, with three arrests made. The student collective's demand for an FIR against the attackers has not been met; instead, 20 individuals, including students and organisers, were booked by Gujarat Police. The involvement of right-wing groups and communal undertones, including demands to 'prove you're not Muslim', indicate a high risk of further clashes. The police response, including taking participants to a police station and filing FIRs against them, suggests a posture that may not protect protesters, increasing the danger for future gatherings. The school's decision to make the books optional and the DEO's directive to sack a consultant show ongoing institutional pressure, which could fuel further protests and counter-protests.
protests.status: A silent reading protest against the removal of Malala Yousafzai's memoir 'I Am Malala' and Anne Frank's 'Diary of a Young Girl' from the reading list of Anand Niketan School was held at a ground in Vastrapur, Ahmedabad, on Thursday evening. The gathering, organised by the Student and Youth Collective, was attacked by alleged VHP and Bajrang Dal activists who disrupted the session, assaulted participants, and demanded they 'prove you're not Muslim'. Three people were arrested following the attack, while the student collective demanded an FIR against the attackers; instead, Gujarat Police filed an FIR against 20 individuals, including students and organisers. The protest ended with participants taken to a police station. The school later made the two books 'optional', and the District Education Officer directed the school to sack a consultant and appoint a principal. Solidarity has since swelled, with reports of 350 voices defending the books, and further legal challenges and reading sessions are planned.

protests.location: Gandhi Maidan to Bihar Chief Minister's Residence, Patna
protests.cause: Protesting against alleged irregularities in the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE-4), including paper leaks, question paper discrepancies, and the controversial detention of a six-year-old child during earlier protests.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical due to confirmed and repeated police violence against protesters. During the latest march from Gandhi Maidan to the CM's residence, thousands of students broke through barricades and clashed with police, who responded with water cannons and lathi charges, resulting in several injuries to protesters and at least two police personnel. Around 25 students were detained, and barbed wire was placed at Dak Bungalow to block the route, with stones reportedly thrown during the confrontation. The administration has imposed heavy security cordons around the CM's residence and key government buildings, and has not conceded the core demands for exam cancellation and re-conduct, keeping tensions elevated. The controversial detention of a six-year-old child during earlier protests has further inflamed public anger, increasing the likelihood of continued confrontations and potential escalation.
protests.status: The Bihar student protest march from Gandhi Maidan to the Chief Minister's residence in Patna remains active and highly volatile. Thousands of BPSC TRE-4 job aspirants began their pre-announced march from Gandhi Maidan but were stopped by police at JP Golambar, where officers used water cannons and lathi charges. Several protesters and at least two police personnel were injured, and around 25 students were detained. Barbed wire was placed at Dak Bungalow to block the route, and stones were reportedly thrown during the confrontation. A delegation of protesters met the Bihar Chief Secretary, and the state suspended the BPSC exam controller over a contentious 'dogs bark' remark. Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav wrote to Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary regarding the ongoing BPSC examination row. The protesters' main demands include a single-tier examination in BPSC-TRE 4 and cancellation of the 70th BPSC exam over alleged paper leaks and irregularities. The administration has not conceded the core demands, and further marches and confrontations remain likely.

protests.cause: App-based cab and bike taxi drivers are protesting against low fare structures, high commission rates charged by ride-hailing platforms, and demanding a revision of fare charts. The protest escalated after police attempted to clear the blockade, leading to violence.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical due to confirmed police violence and mass detentions during the protest on August 19, 2026. Police carried out a lathicharge, after which agitators pelted stones and vandalised over 10 'Ama' buses at Master Canteen Square and PMG Square, resulting in 13 police personnel injured. Arrests escalated from an initial 80 drivers to 113 people arrested and produced before a local court by August 20, 2026, according to police. The use of force by police, combined with stone-pelting and property damage, indicates a highly volatile situation with active enforcement against the protest, which authorities have declared illegal. protests.status: The strike by app-based cab, auto and bike taxi drivers in Bhubaneswar, which began on August 17, 2026, turned violent on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, when protesters pelted stones at police and vandalised government-run 'Ama' buses. According to police, hundreds of protesters took out a rally from Raj Mahal Square and blocked Mahatma Gandhi Marg, with clashes concentrated at Master Canteen Square and PMG Square. Police carried out a lathicharge to disperse the crowd, after which agitators threw stones, injuring 13 police personnel; over 10 'Ama' buses were damaged. Arrests escalated over the following days: initial reports said 80 drivers were detained, while on Thursday, August 20, 2026, Bhubaneswar police stated that 113 people had been arrested and produced before a local court in connection with the violence. The drivers, registered with platforms like Ola, Uber and Rapido, are demanding a fare hike, reduced commission rates, social security and fulfilment of a seven-point charter. Police have deemed the protest illegal and seized vehicles; reports indicate the situation has since returned to normal with vehicular movement resuming, but the drivers' demands remain unaddressed and no formal end to the strike has been announced.

protests.cause: Students are protesting against the repeated leak of question papers for state-level examinations, demanding a thorough investigation, cancellation of compromised exams, and strict action against the leak syndicate. The protest has escalated following a similar demonstration in Bihar where police used water cannons.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the tense standoff between protesters and police at Lower PMG Square, where barricades have been reinforced and additional personnel deployed. Permission for a march to the State Secretariat was denied, increasing the risk of confrontation. The gherao of Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's residence by NSUI activists shows the protest is targeting high-profile locations, which could lead to clashes. While no violence has been reported in Bhubaneswar, the use of water cannon by police in a similar protest in Bihar on August 25 has been cited by organizers, indicating a potential for escalation. The involvement of multiple student and political organizations, including SFI, NSUI, AISF, and Youth Congress, broadens the scope and intensity of the agitation.
protests.status: Student and political organizations continue to protest in Bhubaneswar over alleged examination paper leaks and textbook errors, with gatherings centered at Lower PMG Square. The Odisha Youth Congress held a torch rally (mashal rally) in Bhubaneswar targeting the BJP government over over 3,000 errors in school textbooks and exam paper leaks. Reuters reported that police in Bihar used water cannon and detained dozens of protesters attempting a march, and a separate report indicated that police used water cannons to disperse thousands of youth protesters marching on the state legislature in India. The protests have drawn participation from multiple groups including NSUI, Youth Congress, and SFI, with Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan reportedly joining around 1,500 students. The state government's offer of a committee review has been rejected by protesters who demand immediate cancellation of compromised exams and strict action against leak syndicates. The agitation remains ongoing with no confirmed end date, and similar protests have occurred in other states.
details: Police presence: Barricades reinforced at Lower PMG Square; additional personnel deployed; march to State Secretariat denied permission; no water cannons or tear gas reported in Bhubaneswar.

Recent incidents: Odisha Youth Congress torch rally in Bhubaneswar over textbook errors and exam leaks; NSUI activists gheraoed Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's residence; no violence reported in Bhubaneswar; water cannon and detentions occurred in Bihar on August 25.

protests.name: App-Based Cab and Bike Drivers' Protest Over Fare Regulation
protests.location: Master Canteen Square to Lower PMG Square, Bhubaneswar
protests.cause: App-based cab and bike taxi drivers are demanding fair fare regulation, a fare hike, reduction in application fees, social security benefits, and fair payment for waiting time during rides. They have submitted a seven-point charter of demands to the state government.
protests.dangerReason: The protest escalated into violence on August 19, 2026, with protesters pelting stones at police and vandalising government-run 'Ama' buses at PMG Square, resulting in injuries to 25 protesters and 10 police personnel. Police detained over 100 individuals (reports vary between 50 and 113) and seized vehicles, deeming the protest illegal. The clash occurred at a major arterial junction in Bhubaneswar, and the situation remains tense as drivers continue their strike into its third day. The government has not yet engaged with the protesters' demands, and the crackdown has included vehicle seizures, raising the risk of further escalation. The combination of stone-pelting, property damage, mass detentions, and police injuries confirms a critical danger level.
protests.status: The app-based cab and bike taxi drivers' protest in Bhubaneswar continued into its third day on August 19, 2026, with drivers taking out a rally from Raj Mahal Square and parking vehicles along Mahatma Gandhi Marg, blocking roads and disrupting traffic in the Master Canteen and railway station areas. The strike turned violent on August 19 when protesters allegedly threw stones at police personnel and vandalised government-run 'Ama' buses at PMG Square. Police detained over 100 individuals and seized vehicles, declaring the protest illegal; reports indicate 25 protesters and 10 police personnel were injured in the face-off. The Odisha government has not yet publicly addressed the drivers' seven-point charter of demands, which includes fair fare regulation, a fare hike, reduced application fees, social security benefits, and fair payment for waiting time. The Odisha Online Drivers United Forum has called for continued agitation, and the situation remains tense with the potential for further escalation if talks do not materialise. The strike has also caused ride-hailing prices to surge in Bhubaneswar due to the disruption of app-based services, and commuters struggled to book rides through state-backed mobility platform Odisha Yatri.

protests.location: Muthalapozhi Harbour and Coastal Areas, Thiruvananthapuram
protests.cause: Fishermen and coastal community members are protesting the inadequate search and rescue operations for three fishermen who went missing after separate boat mishaps off the Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam coasts. They are demanding stronger safety measures and compensation for affected families.
protests.dangerReason: The protest remains largely peaceful with no confirmed reports of police violence, mass detentions, or injuries to protesters. protests.status: The search for three fishermen missing since separate boat mishaps on July 31, 2026, off the Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam coasts continued into its ninth day as of August 8, 2026, in the Vizhinjam and Muthalapozhi areas of Thiruvananthapuram district and Neendakara in Kollam district. Families of the missing fishermen, including Shijin (32) of Muthalapozhi, staged rain-soaked protests at Muthalapozhi Harbour and in front of the Vizhinjam Coastal Police Station, demanding intensified search operations and compensation. The Kerala government defended its rescue efforts, and the Chief Minister spoke to the families of the missing fishermen. No reports of violence, mass detentions, or police crackdowns have emerged from the agitation.

protests.name: Anti-NRC-Before-Census Student Solidarity March at Guwahati
protests.location: Cotton University to Dispur Secretariat, GS Road, Guwahati
protests.cause: Students marching in solidarity with the 48-hour Manipur bandh called by JFD demanding NRC update before census. Protesters oppose the government's plan to conduct census enumeration without first updating the NRC, fearing undocumented migrants will be counted as citizens.
protests.dangerReason: The protest directly challenges the central government's census policy and has drawn support from multiple student organizations across Assam, increasing the likelihood of large crowds and potential confrontation with security forces. The 48-hour Manipur bandh has already disrupted enumerator training in Imphal, and similar disruptions are feared in Guwahati. Police have previously used barricades and detentions against NRC-related protests in the city, and the march route passes through sensitive government installations near Dispur Secretariat.

Organizers estimate 500-800 participants, with numbers growing as students from other city colleges join. Police have erected barricades near the Secretariat and are monitoring the march with drone surveillance. Protesters plan to submit a memorandum to the Chief Minister's office demanding suspension of census operations until NRC is updated. No clashes have been reported as of the latest update, but police have warned of detentions if the march breaches prohibited zones.

The Bombay High Court ordered the release of six to seven detainees, citing no BNSS Section 163 restrictions, indicating that detentions were legally questionable. An FIR has been filed against approximately 1,000 unidentified persons for an earlier unlawful assembly at Azad Maidan, and recent solidarity marches led to detentions, including that of CJP supporter Mohammad Danish. The North Goa District Magistrate denied permission for the gathering, and police action included thwarting the protest, creating a volatile environment where further detentions or clashes are plausible.

The Bombay High Court intervened in a special late-night Sunday hearing, ordering the immediate release of six to seven activists, including hotelier Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh, Aditya Parulekar, and Bhupesh Bin, noting that no BNSS Section 163 restrictions were in place. The protest, backed by the 'Enough is Enough' movement and Justice Ferdino Rebello, seeks the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police had earlier filed an FIR against around 1,000 unidentified persons for an unlawful assembly at Azad Maidan, and recent solidarity marches led to detentions, including CJP supporter Mohammad Danish. The situation remains tense, with legal challenges ongoing and the government maintaining a restrictive posture.

The Chief Minister's warning that such protests could sometimes lead to violence further underscores the tense environment.

Valley protest organisers have not publicly responded to the KZC statement, and police have not announced any new deployment tied to it. Observers expect the KZC position to feature in upcoming consultations with the state government and the Census Directorate.

A threatening letter containing two live bullets was sent to two advocates approximately four days before the previous assessment, representing a direct physical threat. The government's refusal to engage, citing sub judice, and the AG's refusal to resign add to the tension.

The lawyers have also engaged in a statewide court boycott and work abstention, with bail and urgent matters exempted. The Meghalaya High Court has issued contempt notices to bar association office-bearers over the boycott, terming the strike 'completely illegal.' Chief Minister Conrad Sangma cited sub judice to deny information in the Assembly regarding the protests, and the Advocate General has refused to step down. The standoff remains unresolved, with no indication of the protest concluding.

protests.location: Routes from Police Bazaar to Dhankheti, Shillong
protests.cause: The Khasi Students' Union (KSU) is protesting against the state government's alleged failure to address long-pending demands related to tribal land rights, employment for local youth, and the government's handling of the ongoing Assam-Meghalaya border dispute, which has led to the current cab blockade and violence.
protests.dangerReason: The KSU black-flag bike rally on August 19, 2026, escalated into violence with assaults, government vehicles burnt, 31 vehicles damaged, and statues of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Swami Vivekananda vandalised in Shillong, confirming property destruction and public disorder. Police arrested three senior KSU leaders — president Raymond Kharjana, vice president Pynkmenlang Sanmiet and general secretary Reuben Najiar — who were sent to judicial custody, and the government has filed 15 FIRs, indicating a firm crackdown. While the situation remains tense with heightened police deployment, there are no confirmed reports of ongoing mass violence or new escalations beyond the August 19-20 incidents, and the KSU's threatened statewide bandh has not been formally confirmed, warranting a high rather than critical danger level.

The rally turned violent, with assaults, government vehicles burnt, and statues of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Swami Vivekananda vandalised; reports indicate 31 vehicles were damaged. Meghalaya Police arrested three top KSU leaders — president Raymond Kharjana, vice president Pynkmenlang Sanmiet and general secretary Reuben Najiar — who were sent to judicial custody. The Meghalaya Government has filed 15 FIRs in connection with the violence, stating the rally had been approved by the East Khasi Hills district administration. Social media users and senior citizens have expressed strong anger and condemnation over the violence and arson that gripped Shillong. The KSU has threatened a statewide bandh, but it has not been formally confirmed. The situation remains tense with heightened police deployment, but no new escalations have been reported since August 20.

protests.name: Ladakh-Wide Bandh Over Delhi Talks Retraction
protests.location: Leh Main Bazaar, Old Town, and Changspa Road; parallel shutdown in Kargil district
protests.cause: Protesters accuse the central government of retracting key constitutional safeguards promised during negotiations with the Ladakh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), including movement toward statehood and Sixth Schedule protections. The shutdown demands transparency on what was actually offered and withdrawn in the Delhi talks.
protests.dangerReason: A full district-wide commercial shutdown in both Leh and Kargil signals coordinated civil disobedience across a sensitive border region, and past Ladakh agitations have escalated into violent clashes with police that left multiple people dead in 2025. The involvement of the Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance means large, organized crowds in confined market areas where police have previously used force and detained demonstrators. With Leh's narrow bazaar lanes and heavy security deployment near the DC office, any attempt to march on government buildings could trigger confrontations.
protests.status: Businesses across Leh and Kargil districts shut down in a coordinated bandh called by the Ladakh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, with shopkeepers in Leh Main Bazaar, Old Town, and Changspa pulling down shutters for the day. The shutdown is a direct response to what organizers call the retraction of key constitutional and political guarantees discussed during talks with Delhi. Markets were largely deserted, with only emergency services and a few pharmacies operating. Police were deployed at major intersections and near the Deputy Commissioner's office to prevent any march toward government premises. Organizers say further phased shutdowns and a delegation to Delhi will follow if the government does not clarify its position in writing.
details: Police deployed in strength at Leh Main Bazaar, Old Town chowk, Changspa Road, and the DC office complex; barricades placed at key intersections, no water cannons visible, drone surveillance reported over the market area.

Shops shuttered across Leh and Kargil on the bandh day; no major clashes reported, but police detained several youth attempting to march toward the DC office; vehicles briefly stopped at Kupchak and Skara checkpoints.

SNM Hospital Leh is the primary facility near the protest zone, roughly 1.5 km from Main Bazaar; no ambulances pre-positioned on site, no injuries reported so far, but narrow lanes could delay emergency access if crowds swell.

Ladakh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance coordinating legal response; local lawyers affiliated with the Ladakh Bar Association on standby; detainees held at Leh police station, no formal FIR details released; organizers say they will challenge detentions in court if not released.

protests.name: Month-Long Martyrs' Remembrance Programme (Aug 24–Sep 24)
protests.location: Leh Main Bazaar to Chowkhang Vihara route; commemorative events at Leh Gate and community halls
protests.cause: A month-long programme to remember those killed in the 2025 Ladakh statehood protest violence, demanding a public inquiry report and accountability for the deaths. It also presses the statehood and Sixth Schedule demands that sparked the original 2025 agitation.
protests.dangerReason: The programme is explicitly commemorative and led by Sonam Wangchuk with candle marches rather than confrontational tactics, reducing immediate clash risk. However, it revives the exact grievance that produced fatal police firing in 2025, and any attempt by authorities to block marches or detain leaders could rapidly escalate. Leh's security establishment remains on edge after the earlier violence, and sustained daily gatherings over a month stretch police capacity and patience.
protests.status: Sonam Wangchuk led a candle march in Leh on the opening day of a month-long remembrance programme running from August 24 to September 24, honoring those killed in the 2025 statehood protest violence. Marchers walked from Main Bazaar toward Chowkhang Vihara holding candles and placards demanding the release of the official inquiry report into the 2025 deaths. Wangchuk said the month will be marked with daily commemorations, public meetings, and a final mass gathering. Police maintained a visible but non-interventionist posture along the route, filming the march. Organizers plan to submit a memorandum to the Deputy Commissioner demanding a time-bound inquiry and compensation for victims' families.
details: Police lined the Main Bazaar–Chowkhang Vihara route with barricades at Leh Gate and Old Town chowk; personnel filmed the march; no water cannons or tear gas deployed; traffic diverted around the march corridor for several hours.

Candle march held peacefully on the opening day with no reported injuries or arrests; earlier in the year, similar statehood protests saw police firing that killed demonstrators, and Wangchuk's hunger strike ended after 26 days over exam paper leak demands.

SNM Hospital Leh is the nearest major facility, about 2 km from the march route; no ambulances stationed on site; organizers have volunteer medics accompanying marches; no injuries reported during the candle march.

Ladakh Apex Body legal cell and local advocates monitoring the programme; no detentions reported during the march; organizers preparing a memorandum to the DC and threatening court action if the 2025 inquiry report is not released; helpline numbers circulated via civil society WhatsApp groups.

protests.name: Punjab Employees & Pensioners 'Maha Bandh' Call
protests.location: Chandigarh-wide: Main gathering at Punjab Raj Bhawan, Sector 3, and Sukhna Lake parking lot
protests.cause: Punjab government employees and pensioners are protesting against the AAP government's failure to implement pending dearness allowance (DA) hikes, pension revisions, and the new pension scheme. They are calling for a statewide shutdown on August 27 to force the government to negotiate.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the massive scale of the protest, with nearly four lakh employees and pensioners expected to participate statewide, creating a high potential for large crowds and possible clashes. The government has declared the bandh illegal and deployed the Rapid Action Force to key government buildings, indicating a strong police presence and readiness for confrontation. Section 144 has been imposed in Chandigarh, banning gatherings of more than five people near the Raj Bhawan, and protesters have defied this order, leading to a tense standoff. Past bandhs in Punjab have seen stone-pelting and bus burning, and with multiple unions and political support from the BJP, the risk of factional clashes and violence remains significant. The cancellation of the CM's meeting with unions further escalates tensions.
protests.status: Punjab government employees and pensioners are preparing for a statewide 'Maha Bandh' on August 27, 2026, with thousands already rallying in Chandigarh over pending 18% DA arrears, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), and regularisation demands. The Bhagwant Mann government has called for talks on August 27, but unions remain firm after the CM cancelled an earlier meeting. The government has declared the bandh illegal and deployed the Rapid Action Force to protect key buildings, while Section 144 restrictions are in place near the Raj Bhawan. Protesters have defied these orders, leading to a tense standoff. The protest has gained political support from BJP leader Partap Singh Bajwa. Unions plan to block entry gates to the Raj Bhawan and Secretariat if demands are not met. A recent protest brought Chandigarh's western sectors to a halt for hours.
details: Police presence: Rapid Action Force deployed to protect key government buildings in Chandigarh; Section 144 imposed near Raj Bhawan, Sector 3, banning gatherings of more than five people; barricades likely at entry points to Raj Bhawan and Secretariat.

protests.cause: The march, backed by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) and Qaumi Insaaf Morcha, demands the release of Sikh prisoners held in jails across Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh. The protest has gained urgency after a jailed extremist's video surfaced on August 20, 2026, calling for a mass mobilization.

The circulation of a jailed extremist's video on August 20, 2026, urging supporters to 'break barriers' adds a radical element, increasing the risk of violence. Historical precedent from 2024 and 2025 marches, which saw baton charges and tear gas near the Raj Bhavan, further supports the critical assessment.
protests.status: The Bandi Sikh March in Chandigarh, backed by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) and Qaumi Insaaf Morcha, remains an active and volatile protest as of late August 2026. The march to Punjab Raj Bhavan was denied permission, and a large police deployment, including RAF and paramilitary units, was in place. Protesters have vowed to continue their agitation, with SGPC announcing a parallel peaceful sit-in if blocked.

The morcha has called for a Punjab Bandh on August 21, 2026, which saw a mixed response across the state, with tight security at the Chandigarh-Mohali border and disruptions to normal life. The protest has received backing from the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC), adding to its strength. Protesters are demanding the release of Sikh prisoners (Bandi Singhs) who have completed their sentences, including parole for those convicted in the Beant Singh assassination case.
